facts.statement: Mwalau walterlinii is the only known species within the extinct genus Mwalau.
facts.quote: Mwalau walterlinii is an extinct species of megapode from Vanuatu, and the only species in the genus Mwalau.

facts.statement: The single known specimen of Mwalau was found at the Teouma archaeological site on the island of Efate.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen is from the Teouma archeological site on the island of Efate.

facts.statement: Mwalau had body proportions similar to the Australian brushturkey and was capable of flight.
facts.quote: It was built in similar proportion to the extant Australian brushturkey, and, like that species, could fly.

facts.statement: Mwalau was larger than living megapodes but smaller than the extinct giant malleefowl.
facts.quote: It is distinguishable from other extant megapodes by its large size, though it is smaller than the extinct giant malleefowl.

facts.statement: The species name honors Walter Lini, the first Prime Minister of Vanuatu.
facts.quote: The scientific and common name honor the first Prime Minister of Vanuatu, Walter Lini.

facts.statement: The genus name Mwalau is derived from the Laipta language term for megapodes.
facts.quote: The name of the genus comes from the Laipta name for megapodes.

facts.statement: Mwalau belongs to the family Megapodiidae.
Mwalau is classified as a reptile.
Mwalau lived during the Holocene epoch, between 0.0117 and 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Holocene to Holocene (0.0117 to 0 million years ago)
